Equations that contain partial derivatives are called *partial differential equations}, or PDEs.

PDEs arise frequently in models of structured populations, physics (and therefore physical biology!), and a great many other real-world phenomena.

Note that in these equations, I have included the independent variables explicitly in some cases but left them implicit in others.
That is common practice in the literature because including all of them all of the time can lead to long equations that are difficult to read.

A compromise is to do as I have done above, which is to include the independent variables the first time a dependent variable is used but not otherwise (unless to indicate particular values of the independent variables).
That makes for clearer reading, but it means that you must keep track in your mind of which independent variables govern each dependent variable.
